about: The `report_anomalies` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2021 only.

rows.detail: Two printed inconsistencies survive: the grade 10 row's resident and total figures (104 and 113) leave a school choice figure of 9 that is not printed, and the High School Total's resident figure (450) does not equal its grade rows (120+104+125+101 = 450 -- it does; but 450+23 = 473, and the individual totals 122+113+125+113 = 473 as well, so the missing grade 10 school choice figure is 9).
Absent since FY2019: Belmont Savings Bank, an 'OPEB' cash line, and the Fidelity ARRA/Senior grant accounts persist at a few dollars.
NO AMOUNT COLUMN SURVIVES -- the table as rendered carries only recipient and project title, so the grants cannot be valued from this text.

The assessors' table on p38 does not tie to itself: the four class valuations sum to 1,742,668,758 against a printed Totals of 1,548,256,450, and the four levies sum to 29,956,477.18 against a printed 28,054,406.88. Separately the narrative on the same page says the FY2021 rate is $17.74 while the table says 17.19. The report gives two tax rates and two totals for the same year.

rows.table: Fiscal 2021 assessments and revenues by major class
rows.detail: READ THE TOTALS ROW WITH CARE -- IT DOES NOT TIE TO ITS OWN COLUMNS.
Note some sub-lines do not sum to their stated totals (arrests 142+254+11 = 407 does;
IDENTICAL TO THE FY2020 LIMITS VOTED THREE YEARS EARLIER (FY2019 report, p159), fund for fund and in total.
Unlike the FY2019 report this year does NOT reprint the full six-column table of purposes, revenue sources and restrictions -- the article refers instead to Chapter 138 of the General By-laws.
STILL LARGELY UNUSABLE as charts, but the p74 expense pie duplicates the p73 table which IS complete, so nothing is lost there.

The communicable disease table on p85 prints 'Novel Coronavirus (SARS, MERS, etc.) 1105' as one line among eleven ordinary diseases that together total 43. In the same year Influenza fell from 48 cases (FY2019) to 10.

The special revenue funds schedule is the cleanest published account of COVID money in either report, and every programme has its own named line: ARPA $614,195.58 received and entirely unspent at year end, FY21 School Reopening #102 $377,550.00, FY21 ESSER #113 $197,973.00, Covid Prevention Grant $67,075.00, Remote Learning Tech $55,735.00, and FEMA #4496 - COVID Grant carrying a NEGATIVE $74,911.81 balance, i.e. the town was that far ahead of reimbursement.

The employee gross wages table is fully legible here -- over 400 named amounts -- and almost entirely amountless in FY2019. Whatever went wrong with the FY2019 payroll pages is specific to that document and was not the rotation.

The Turkey Hill Elementary staff roster ends with two headcount lines, 'Admin =2.0' and 'Paraprofessionals = 12'. Published headcount is one of the project's standing unanswered questions, and one school prints two lines of it at the bottom of a staff list.

The Veterans' Services report on p79 states plainly that the Town pays out benefits and is then reimbursed 75% by the state, 'the maximum allowable share' -- $71,999.46 paid, $53,999.60 reimbursed. That is a budget line being netted down by a reimbursement, said out loud, in the report itself.

The FY2021 Annual Town Meeting was held on 13 June 2020, not on the first Saturday in May as the town facts panel states -- visible only in the capital projects fund's article references ('6 6/20 ATM'). The May 2021 meeting in the town clerk's section is the FY2022 one.

The debt repayment schedule recovered its grand totals in FY2021 and did not in FY2019, which means the town's forward debt-service profile ($4,516,558 in FY2022 falling to $2,547,440 by FY2026) is quotable from this report and not from that one.

The FY2021 report prints no vital records report. Its own contents page lists one at folio 137, and FY2019 prints births, deaths and marriages. There is nothing at that folio but the town meeting record.

NOTE: the contents page lists a 'Vital Records Report' at folio 137, but folio 137 (PDF p138) carries the Annual Town Meeting record and NO vital records report appears anywhere in the document -- unlike FY2019, which prints one.
The FY2022 capital plan prints TWO priority columns -- the Town Manager's and the Capital Planning Committee's -- and they disagree on the top three items. FY2019's capital plan has only one.

rows.table: FY 2022 capital plan (Capital Planning Committee report)
rows.detail: First, it carries TWO priority columns -- the Town Manager's and the Capital Planning Committee's -- and they disagree: Turnout Gear is CPC priority 1 but TM priority 2, Bulletproof Vests CPC 2 but TM 3.
Monty Tech's grant income more than doubled in the pandemic, from $945,083 in FY2019 to $2,037,076 in FY2021 -- and that figure is on the one page of the report that OCR'd fully mirrored (p125).
Technology $30,000 (OCR'd '530,000').

rows.table: FY 2022 capital plan (as voted, Annual Town Meeting Article 5)
rows.detail: The two printings agree project for project with p96 -- as in FY2019, the apparent divergence between the committee's copy and the town meeting's copy is an OCR artefact, not a real difference.
As in FY2019 several line numbers and account names did not OCR (line 13 Reserve Fund reads '75000000' for $75,000.00) and the OCR turns line numbers 8 and 9 into '∞ a'.

rows.table: Town and school employee gross wages, calendar 2021
rows.detail: Two caveats before using it: a handful of figures carry OCR digit damage (a comma read as a full stop, '15,718,68'), and gross wages include overtime, details and stipends, so a figure here is not a salary and not a full employment cost.
SAME LIMITATION AS FY2019: the rendering hard-clips at 188 characters and every AMOUNT in the third column is cut off, though the labels survive.
FEDERAL REVENUE is the one that matters most in a COVID year and it is exactly the one clipped.
One value carries an OCR space: '$26, 138.82'.
Note 'OPES TRUST' and 'SEWER OPE TRUST' are OCR corruptions of OPEB.
